judgment_calls: Could have cut at L796 (end of 'Ignore untrusted data' section) and L1107 (end of span) as I did, or at L698 (end of 'Assume best intentions' section) and L796. The cuts at section boundaries are clean because each section is self-contained and the only crossing linkages are the seeded concepts (chain of command, scope of autonomy) and cross-references to other sections, which are handled as dangling needs.

The 'Stay in bounds' section (L797-1107) is large (311 lines) but is a single cohesive unit with a clear internal structure (comply with laws, disallowed content, and sub-rules). Dividing it further would risk cutting through the internal cross-references (e.g., transformation exception, sexual content, info hazards, privacy) that are established and used within the section. I chose to keep it as one child and let its leaf decomposition handle the internal structure.

I seeded the section names (e.g., stay_in_bounds_section, highlight_misalignments_section, etc.) because they are used as cross-references across children and need canonical names for the graph to link them. These are not established in this span but are referenced, so they are seeded as dangling needs for the parent to resolve.

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: The ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts.

seed_vocabulary.name: assistant_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: The assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document.

seed_vocabulary.name: conversation_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: A conversation is a list of messages, each containing a role and content; roles determine authority of instructions.

seed_vocabulary.name: message_role_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: The role of a message (system, developer, user, assistant, tool) specifies its source and determines authority in conflicts.

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command_principle
seed_vocabulary.prose: The principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control.

seed_vocabulary.name: scope_of_autonomy
seed_vocabulary.prose: The agreed-upon boundary of the assistant's autonomy, defining which sub-goals it may pursue, acceptable side effects, and when it must pause for clarification or approval.

seed_vocabulary.name: stay_in_bounds_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that describes limits on the assistant's behavior, including scenarios where the assistant should refrain from fully complying with a request.

seed_vocabulary.name: highlight_misalignments_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that discusses how the assistant should highlight misalignments or disagreements with user or developer instructions.

seed_vocabulary.name: letter_and_spirit_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that discusses the distinction between the letter and the spirit of instructions.

seed_vocabulary.name: control_side_effects_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that discusses how the assistant should control side effects of its actions.

seed_vocabulary.name: ask_clarifying_questions_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that discusses when and how the assistant should ask clarifying questions.

seed_vocabulary.name: risk_taxonomy_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that categorizes risks and describes the assistant's responsibilities in balancing empowerment and harm minimization.

seed_vocabulary.name: red_line_principles_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that describes the red line principles that the assistant must uphold, including legal constraints and safety-critical information.

seed_vocabulary.name: assume_best_intentions_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that describes the implicit biases the assistant should apply when interpreting ambiguous instructions.

seed_vocabulary.name: refusal_style_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that describes how the assistant should style refusals.

seed_vocabulary.name: no_agenda_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that describes the principle that the assistant should not pursue its own agenda beyond helping the user.

seed_vocabulary.name: transformation_exception_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that describes the exception allowing transformation of user-provided restricted content.

seed_vocabulary.name: sexual_content_involving_minors_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that prohibits sexual content involving minors.

seed_vocabulary.name: information_hazards_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that prohibits providing detailed, actionable steps for carrying out activities that are illicit, could harm people or property, or lead to critical or large-scale harm.

seed_vocabulary.name: protect_privacy_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that prohibits responding to requests for private or sensitive information about people.
